name: Fortis
headline: A North American group of regulated electricity and gas delivery utilities earning steady, regulator-set returns.
what_short: Regulated electricity and gas utilities, North America
what_it_does: Fortis owns ten regulated utilities in five Canadian provinces, ten US states and Grand Cayman, delivering electricity and gas. About 95% of its assets are power lines and gas pipes for transmission and distribution. Regulators set the prices it may charge.
why_it_passed: Its utilities are franchises, so customers have no alternative supplier of their power or gas.
Regulated assets are virtually all of its assets, and the return on its common equity was a steady 7.1% to 7.7% a year from 2021 to 2025.
Added capital earns the allowed return, which the analysis counts as a decent, though not excellent, use of money.
Its credit ratings are solid: S&P A- as issuer, and the outlook moved from negative to stable in November 2025.
why_not_now: A regulator caps what a utility may earn, so the price is far above what that capped return justifies. At C$80.99 a share the cash the business produces is only 3.75% of the price, less than the 4.19% on a long Government of Canada bond, and the analysis's fair price is C$28.96.
watch: Total debt is C$34.6 billion, with earnings covering interest and preferred dividends only about 1.9 to 2.0 times.
The holding company has no revenue of its own and serves its debt from subsidiary dividends.
Moody's withdrew its ratings in January 2026 at the company's request.
